name: Deep tissue filler injection

card.summary: Placing filler in deeper facial layers, near bone or in fat pads, to build structure and projection in areas such as the chin, cheeks and jawline.
card.note: Performed by trained injectors; vascular complications are documented.

quick.overview:
Deep tissue filler injection refers to placing dermal filler beneath the skin's upper layers, in deep fat or on the bone, rather than in the dermis. Firmer fillers placed this deep add structural support and projection, which is how people use them for chin, cheek and jaw definition.

Fillers are widely used and studied in registered trials, while the specific question of depth is mostly addressed within anatomy and safety literature. Practitioners describe deep placement as shaping contour, whereas superficial placement softens lines.
quick.how: A licensed injector places a firm hyaluronic acid or similar filler in a deeper plane, sometimes using a cannula, after assessing facial anatomy. Results are typically described as immediate, with swelling settling over days to weeks.
quick.risks: Bruising, swelling and lumps are common. Rarely, filler entering a blood vessel can cause tissue death or vision loss, and anatomic studies describe pathways to the ophthalmic artery. Regulators in many places restrict filler to medical professionals.

lead: Deep tissue filler injection means depositing dermal filler in deeper planes of the face, such as the deep fat compartments or just above the periosteum, rather than in the superficial or mid dermis. Wikipedia notes that firmer fillers go into deeper tissue to give structural support, while softer gels go superficially to treat fine lines [1].

For appearance, deep placement is used to add projection and definition to the chin, cheeks, temples and jawline, effects that superficial filler does not produce [1]. Published work includes a cosmetic dermatology paper on non-surgical facial reshaping with structured injection points called MD Codes [2].
Safety research focuses on facial vessels: anatomic studies map arteries around the lips and the route by which cosmetic injections can reach the ophthalmic artery [3][4].

chain: Firm filler placed in deep layer
Adds volume and projection at bone or deep fat
Sharper chin, cheek or jaw contour
angle.text: Deep placement changes contour by building support under the soft tissue, which is why it is used for chin, cheek and jaw shape.

paras: Fillers are natural or synthetic hydrogels such as hyaluronic acid, many crosslinked with BDDE. Placement depth varies by product and goal [1].

Common effects are bruising, redness and pain; rare serious events include embolization into ophthalmic and retinal arteries that can cause blindness, and delayed skin necrosis [1]. Anatomic studies describe the arterial pathway to the ophthalmic artery after cosmetic injection and the typical pattern of the labial arteries [3][4].
In the US fillers are regulated as medical devices requiring a provider, while in the EEA and UK they are non-prescription devices with CE marking [1].

Registered trials have evaluated various hyaluronic acid fillers for the face, including a pilot using ultrasound and histology of HA gel in adipose tissue and a study of a filler for cheek augmentation [5][6]. These are not designed to compare injection depths.
